<thought>The mass spectrum shows isotopic pattern consistent with one chlorine and one bromine (M at 233.96 Da, M‑2 at 231.96 Da). The 13C NMR indicates a para‑disubstituted phenyl ring (four aromatic carbon signals, two pairs of equivalent carbons) plus three aliphatic carbons (≈ 49 ppm, 26 ppm, 11 ppm). The ¹H NMR shows a methyl (0.85 ppm, 3 H), a methylene (2.04 ppm, 2 H), a deshielded methine (4.62 ppm, 1 H) attached to chlorine, and four aromatic protons (7.46 ppm). This matches a para‑bromophenyl ring bearing a 1‑chloro‑2‑propyl side chain. The molecular formula derived from the data is C₉H₁₀ClBr, which fits the observed mass. The corresponding SMILES string is `Brc1ccc(cc1)C(Cl)CC`. This SMILES is valid and represents the described structure.</thought>
<final_answer>Brc1ccc(cc1)C(Cl)CC</final_answer>
